claims.text: EAM references have poor configurational representation of multicomponent HEA liquids near melting.
Replacing an EAM reference with a machine-learning interatomic potential trained on solid and liquid ab initio data will overcome this poor liquid-state representation.
The proposed machine-learning reference will reduce reference–target Hamiltonian mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The intervention is applicable to CoCrFeMnNi or similar three- to five-component high-entropy alloys.
A neural-network or Gaussian approximation potential can be used as the thermodynamic-integration reference in place of EAM.
The proposed applicability range is within approximately 150–200 K of melting for compositions containing at least three principal elements.
The method requires single-phase stability over the relevant temperature range.
The machine-learning potential can capture a broader diversity of local atomic configurations than EAM in high-temperature solid and liquid phases.
The machine-learning potential can capture relevant many-body interactions in high-temperature solid and liquid phases.
Improved representation of configurations and many-body interactions will increase overlap between configuration spaces sampled by the reference and ab initio Hamiltonians.
Greater reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The machine-learning reference will reduce the reference-to-ab-initio free-energy difference by on the order of tens of meV per atom relative to EAM.
The predicted reduction applies to both solid and near-melting liquid states.
TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references exhibit larger free-energy discrepancies when describing the liquid phase.
Performance improvements may diminish outside the machine-learning potential's composition and temperature training domain.
Phase separation or ordering outside the training regime may diminish performance improvements.
